findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the scope claim: adding `ran_model` to the sidecar row changes each corpus's manifest `content_hash` (computed over all row items in `_compute_manifest`) and the cache filename; note this expected fingerprint shift rather than asserting no manifest impact.
evidence: Plan: 'it does not change any existing row's other fields or the manifest schema.'

corpus.py:302 `[{k: v for k, v in row.items()} for row in sorted(rows, key=_sort_key)]` then `content_hash = hashlib.sha256(payload...)` — the hash covers ALL row keys, so a new `ran_model` key alters it
content_hash is emitted in the manifest (corpus.py:317) and drives the cache filename (corpus.py:323), so it is a same-file consumer of row shape
findings.finding: Plan claims the additive `ran_model` row key 'does not change any existing row's other fields or the manifest schema,' but `_compute_manifest` computes `content_hash` over every key/value pair of every row (`{k: v for k, v in row.items()}` with `sort_keys=True`), so adding `ran_model` to each emitted row will change the manifest `content_hash` for every corpus.
findings.location: Approach — 'Corpus field addition needed by this ticket's own tests...' paragraph; corpus.py `_compute_manifest` (lines 301-306)
scenarios: Regenerating the corpus after this edit produces a different `content_hash`/cache filename than the pre-edit corpus, invalidating any cached artifact or hash-pinned test that assumed the old value
findings.suggested_fix: Reword the corpus paragraph to acknowledge that the additive key changes every corpus's `content_hash` (and cache-file name), while leaving the manifest key set and other row values unchanged; flag any hash-pinned tests/fixtures that must be regenerated.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that resolve_pinned_model composes on the existing production resolvers (model_classes.load_class_slots + resolve_class for the primary id, resolve_fallback_chain for the dropped fallback) rather than re-reading rebar.toml directly, so the pinned/attested id matches production's CLI>env>config precedence and provider-qualification.
evidence: Plan: 'reads rebar.toml\'s [llm.model_classes] for that class\'s model field, requires the resolved id to be a Bedrock id (str.startswith("bedrock:"))'

model_classes.py:298-304 resolve_class(name, slots) returns the primary provider:model string; :307-313 resolve_fallback_chain(name, slots) returns the fallback chain; :316-332 load_class_slots(repo_root) is 'THE integration point' that pulls the model_classes sub-table and applies env/CLI overrides via _parse_slot (:178-199)

Because resolve_class already returns 'bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8' as-is for an already-qualified id, the startswith('bedrock:') check works cleanly on top of the existing resolver; a bespoke TOML read is strictly more code and less faithful to production
The parity guard's whole purpose is to match production model selection, so any divergence from the production resolution path is a soundness risk, not a style preference
findings.finding: resolve_pinned_model is specified to 'read rebar.toml's [llm.model_classes] for that class's model field' directly, rather than composing on the existing production resolvers (model_classes.load_class_slots / resolve_class / resolve_fallback_chain); a direct TOML read would bypass the CLI>env>config-table>default precedence and provider-qualification those helpers apply, so the parity guard could attest a model id that differs from the one production actually resolves.
findings.location: Approach > Pinned targets ('reads rebar.toml's [llm.model_classes] for that class's model field')
scenarios: An operator sets REBAR_LLM_FRONTIER_MODEL or a `-c llm.frontier.model=...` override in a run: the production runner honors it via _parse_slot, but a direct-TOML resolve_pinned_model would ignore it and pin/attest the stale rebar.toml value
A future config uses a bare (unqualified) model id relying on provider inference: resolve_class composes the provider via _resolve_target, a direct .get('model') read would not
findings.suggested_fix: In Approach > Pinned targets, replace 'reads rebar.toml's [llm.model_classes] for that class's model field ... and drops any fallback candidate' with: resolve the class via slots = model_classes.load_class_slots(repo_root); primary = model_classes.resolve_class(class_name, slots); assert primary.startswith('bedrock:'); the fallback (model_classes.resolve_fallback_chain) is deliberately discarded so the composed in-process chain is the single homogeneous [primary] candidate.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Have resolve_pinned_model compose on model_classes.load_class_slots + resolve_class (and resolve_fallback_chain for the drop-fallback step) rather than reading the raw [llm.model_classes] `model` field, so provider-qualification, env overrides, and the config-merge/degradation are inherited, not re-implemented.
evidence: Plan: resolve_pinned_model 'reads rebar.toml's [llm.model_classes] for that class's model field ... and drops any fallback candidate'

src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py:298 resolve_class(name, slots) returns the primary provider:model string; :307 resolve_fallback_chain returns the chain; :316 load_class_slots reads the real config table
model_classes.py:319-323 docstring: 'without this entry point ... every consumer would re-invent the extraction' — the exact anti-pattern this plan re-introduces
Raw model-field read bypasses _resolve_target's provider-qualification/validation and the env-override + user<project merge that load_class_slots inherits
findings.finding: resolve_pinned_model re-implements model-class resolution that model_classes.py already provides (load_class_slots + resolve_class + resolve_fallback_chain), by reading the raw [llm.model_classes] `model` field directly and dropping fallback by hand.
scenarios: A frontier slot configured with a provider= key but a bare model id resolves differently through raw-field read than through resolve_class, producing a non-provider-qualified id the Bedrock startswith check then mis-judges
An operator env override (REBAR_LLM_FRONTIER_MODEL) is silently ignored because the raw table read skips the override precedence load_class_slots applies
findings.suggested_fix: resolve_pinned_model: slots = model_classes.load_class_slots(); resolved = model_classes.resolve_class(PASS_MODEL_CLASS[pass_name], slots); require resolved.startswith('bedrock:'); the homogeneous chain is simply resolve_class's primary with resolve_fallback_chain(...) dropped.
